cases.scope: CI-only Windows2022 patched GLib/GIO; registry versus nochange, 0-16 epochs
cases.observed: Original #45015173260 private +221184B, optional REGION +155648B, heap BUSY -7794B; three independent GIO16 runs corroborated signs, not owners. Synthetic Windows2022 calibration #45040046000: controlled test HeapAlloc64/HeapFree48, 16 expected outstanding; ETW started before workload, sequential capture, logger zero-loss checked, xperf totals+size360 stack action PASS. This is NOT a recorded actual exact-16 xperf table count nor any real GIO owner. NEW 2026-11-23 synthetic ETW source-calibration Windows #45044677361 independently matched unique noinline source stack: 64 HeapAlloc(360) calls, 48 frees, 16 intentionally retained (=5,760 requested bytes); zero reported event/log buffer loss. Process-wide 360B size-filter saw ~78-85 total allocations, 16 outstanding; global Alloc KB/count semantics not identical. Proof is ONLY synthetic and NOT GIO leak attribution. 2026-11-23 actual disposable MSVC GIO runtime #45046446784: nochange watch registrations=6, APC completions=0, final pending=6/peak=6; registry 16cycles registrations=23, APC completions=17, final pending=6/peak=6; GIO SDK exports=2047 matched. This is direct *registry watch subscription* bounded-lifetime evidence, NOT overall GIO PrivateUsage leak classification. 2026-11-23 isolated Windows Xperf 16-cycle preworkload CI #45051751198: nochange new HeapAlloc 32101/outstanding0 (stack coverage100%). #45052226913: nochange new HeapAlloc32095/outstanding0; registry 16 cycles completed but HeapSession disappeared at precleanup even with 512MB sequential limit, so REGISTRY owner unknown. Source-guarded last4-of16 CI #45052837535: nochange HeapAlloc8050/out0, complete stack count coverage; registry 4-cycle late capture and loss check/Xperf stack report generation succeeded but original source-stack table parser rejected. Zero nochange outstanding only for events within window, NOT process-wide all alloc/VirtualAlloc or an actual leak-zero proof. Nov23 isolated Windows #45053779999 late4-of16 nochange Alloc=8049 Out=0; registry Alloc=619727, Out=16061, Xperf OutKB=890.8; zero loss and precleanup interval, but top1024 full-stack parser rejected. Follow-up Windows #45058803441 separately reproduces nochange 8050/0 and registry 619729/16061 OutKB=890.8, proving numerical repeatability in the SAME 4-of-16 scoped type of run, NOT a leaked GIO object. Of 1024 Xperf stack rows, 31 violated Out#<=Alloc#; strict parser accepted 993 rows representing 15595 outstanding blocks, leaving 466 registry outstanding outside validated stack rows. The 1024-row limit was reached; missing 466 may be invalid rows and/or omitted top-k rows. No causal owner or global APC idle proven. Repeat #45059395512 / #45059995357 registry last4 Xperf Out#=16061 OutKB≈890.8 KiB, nochange Out#=0; 15595 wellformed GIO-containing stack outstanding, 466 unknown; 30 invalid Out>Alloc top1024 rows. Same-run #45059995357 PrivateUsage registry-control0_16 +139264 B, REGION+69632 B, BUSY-3658 B; registry 17 callbacks,18 workers, worker_active_after_cleanup=1,worker_active_final=0, quiescence_proven=0. Independent numeric-only archived CI #45060607547 PASS verifies original artifact and distinct window scopes.
cases.why_previous_did_not_resolve: HeapWalk BUSY and REGION are different from PSAPI PrivateUsage; former only reports current blocks/selected regions. Prior ETW saved truncated top25 module frame occurrences, not matched allocation+free bytes or a complete call-site owner. Unproven worker quiescence biases endpoints. The corrected #45040046000 probe closes pre-workload event-start, circular overwrite, and missing local-symbol setup ONLY on a synthetic fixture. The filtered report has not yet been independently parsed into exact 16 outstanding / 5760 requested bytes and matching source stack, nor adapted to real GIO workload and global worker quiet boundary. Follow-up diagnosed that this WPT version's combined `-stacks -size 360 361` yielded no stack frames although unfiltered `-stacks -top 100` contained the synthetic symbol. `-totals -size ... -requireframes` did not isolate source count (e.g., 84 vs known64). Local parser now verifies unfiltered unique-source stack 64/16, so that synthetic gap is FIXED. No proof yet of true GIO owner across completed worker epochs. The watch subscription submechanism IS NOW bounded by both pinned source and runtime counts; previously only a source-level model had been available. It cannot explain the remaining owner-unknown GIO/WinRT and COM/heap commit residuals. Do not rerun watch bound as if unproven. Existing 256/512MB full-registry sequential ETW stopped HeapSession before safe stop, making owner inference impossible. New last4-of16 capture fixed logger exhaustion but revealed an Xperf source stack report shape/coverage difference. Previous parser did not preserve a safe error classification or independently extract aggregate Out# on failure; this is a diagnostic-instrument limitation, not a proven leak or an unexplained endpoint. Two genuine registry late-window captures are now available, unlike the earlier missing HeapSession. Full stack attribution still failed because 31 of 1024 Xperf rows reported Out#>Alloc# and top-1024 count was saturated; a further 466 outstanding blocks cannot be assigned to a validated stack. This is no longer generic 'unknown': specific Xperf row semantics and top-N truncation are the active diagnostic defects. The independent Xperf heap totals DO establish 16061 outstanding in both runs, not their expected lifetime. Avoid treating bad rows as OTHER or silently accepting out>alloc. The top-frame-image fallback does not match Xperf total/stack output; sanitized diagnostics #45059995357 show global_headers=0,top_headers=0,alloc_lines=0,one dash part. Thus treating its absence as no images would be false. 15595 source-GIO-containing stack live counts are real during incomplete lifetime; after_cleanup had active AppInfo worker, so no proof they had outlived intended work. Private0→16 and ETW13→16 cannot be causally subtracted.
cases.missing_observable: Explicit post-worker lifetime boundary showing whether the source-GIO-containing in-window allocations were freed after AppInfo work completion (or persisted after an independently justified closed producer epoch), with untruncated owner coverage for remaining 466; same-PID aligned PrivateUsage/Heap REGION at each lifecycle boundary. Existing Xperf top1024 and -images output cannot close that gap.
cases.next_automatic_action: Use #45060607547 saved numeric reconcilation as baseline; DO NOT remeasure old window. Audit existing AppInfo phase trace and CI timing fence to design bounded, explicitly post-worker scope with its own enter/exit gates and no false global APC quiet claim. Only build/run Windows once it records NEW expected-lifetime evidence compared with #45059995357; source-specific owner census must fail closed on 466 unknown, top1024 truncation and possibly pending callbacks. Record actual worker timing at ETW start/stop rather than infer from after_cleanup. If no reliable callback producer barrier exists, classify open and document exact alternative measurable event.
cases.decisive_rule: Nochange 0 and registry 16061 are observed newly allocated Win32 heap live blocks at ETW stop last4/16, not process-wide leaks. Worker_active_after_cleanup=1 and worker_active_final=0 from the same run make expected-lifetime proof incomplete, not leak confirmation; source-validated GIO stack 15595 not direct owner, 466 unknown. Classify LEAK_CONFIRMED only after owner source and post-expected-lifetime unfreed growth at comparable windows; bounded retention requires plateau and heap free/commit reconciliation. Until then evidence_gap.

cases.scope: CI-only Windows registry callbacks and GIO worker/APC parser cleanup
cases.observed: Archived phase trace reports worker_active_after_cleanup=1 and boundary_tick_ambiguous=1; 0-18 paired windows are not globally quiescent. Windows runtime #45046446784 shows APC delivery completed 17 times in registry 16-cycle arm, with 23 total re-registrations and 6 pending watches at the end. A pending watched key is normal: fully global APC queue idle NOT proven. Same-run #45059995357 shows actual registry17 callbacks,18 worker instances, worker_active_after_cleanup=1, worker_active_final=0, boundary_tick_ambiguous=1; registry watch six pending bounded. Narrow ETW stop BEFORE cleanup means this snapshot does not directly establish busy worker at ETW endpoint.
cases.why_previous_did_not_resolve: A finished AppInfo update counter does not acknowledge not-yet-delivered APCs or globally drain other async producers. Timed wait and GObject count alone can produce false leak/plateau conclusions. Even an observed per-key watch count bound is not a closed producer queue or worker quiescence acknowledgment. Watch counts quantify one source cohort only, and do not drain Windows APC or unrelated WinRT callbacks. Even though the later phase trace observed a worker actively completing after cleanup, the recorded ETW stop was earlier (precleanup), so current instrumentation cannot map each ETW-outstanding allocation to a proved finished lifetime. Another 2s idle wait is not a globally closed callback producer barrier.
cases.missing_observable: Proven closed producer/consumer boundary, including callback arrivals, queued jobs, active worker count, update epoch completion and absence of delayed callback after snapshot.
cases.next_automatic_action: Re-use existing same-run phase trace and source CI fences; design a bounded post-worker-completion observation with explicit callback epoch acknowledgement, separate worker-active-at-ETW-stop metric, and unambiguous APC delivered-window status. Run only in disposable Windows CI after fail-closed source/selftests, not the real host. Never call arbitrary SleepEx elapsed time global quiescence.
cases.decisive_rule: Worker active_after_cleanup=1 and worker_active_final=0 in #45059995357 prove activity at one later lifecycle marker, not global APC idle and not the exact ETW stop. Only a measured post-worker closure and source allocation lifetime can classify leak vs expected retention; current case stays OPEN.
